heroDescription: The Hitelecom H100 is a signal coupling accessory for selected 2.4 GHz or 5.8 GHz RF paths. Use the connected radio, antenna, cable assembly and installation drawing to define the required component configuration. Applications range from packaged monitoring equipment to process-plant retrofits, with RF performance verified for the complete path. Hazardous-area use requires the applicable certificate, marking and installation conditions for the exact supplied assembly.

featureIntro: An accessory belongs in a complete interface specification: the operating band, connected equipment, RF budget, mechanical arrangement and applicable installation documentation. The H100 provides no sensing, protocol conversion or cellular connection of its own.

features.title: Selected 2.4 GHz / 5.8 GHz paths
features.text: Start with the actual radio operating frequencies. Identify the required version and usable bandwidth rather than assuming that every frequency between the two published bands is supported.

features.title: Defined equipment interfaces
features.text: Specify connector series, gender, polarity, mating arrangement and cable construction. Include drawings of both connected ends so the component can be assessed as part of the assembly.

features.title: RF loss and matching criteria
features.text: Set acceptance requirements for insertion loss and port matching over the operating band, together with permitted RF input power. Numerical H100 values require the corresponding technical record.

features.title: Antenna-path assessment
features.text: Account for cables, connectors and antenna gain in the system design. Any applicable RF-power restrictions belong to the complete installation, not only to the coupling accessory.

features.title: Environmental assembly review
features.text: IP68 is the published housing reference. Define immersion conditions, connector sealing, cable support and exposure for the installed version; a housing rating does not describe every joint.

features.title: Mechanical integration
features.text: Published mounting options include lugs, pole clamps and slotted arrangements. Select the supplied hardware around connector access, cable bend radius, service clearance and mechanical loading.

features.title: Hazardous-area documentation
features.text: Match the exact certificate, marking and instructions to the jurisdiction, gas or dust group, area classification and temperature requirements. The product name alone does not establish intrinsic safety or approval.

features.title: Repeatable configuration records
features.text: Record the part revision, radio and antenna references, cable drawing and verification method. These details give prototype, installation and replacement work a common acceptance baseline.

planningIntro: Bring the RF interface drawing and installation requirements into the same selection review. Keep component performance, system approval and communications coverage as separate engineering questions.

planning.title: Map the RF chain
planning.text: Identify the radio output, coupling component, cables, intermediate connectors and antenna. Record band, permitted input power, matching requirements and the loss allowed between the equipment and antenna.

planning.title: Review the installed environment
planning.text: Describe the mounting position, exposure, ambient limits, chemical contact and maintenance arrangements. For a classified area, supply the required approval basis and the complete equipment arrangement.

planning.title: Set an acceptance baseline
planning.text: Agree which RF measurements and installed-equipment checks demonstrate compatibility. Keep traceable settings, cable references and results so any replacement or design change can be compared with the accepted configuration.
planning.brief: Measurement method · Acceptance limits · Installed check · Revision record

faqs.q: What role does the H100 perform?
faqs.a: It is a signal coupling accessory within a selected 2.4 GHz or 5.8 GHz RF path. The equipment specification identifies the radio, antenna, cable interfaces and required component performance.

faqs.q: Is the H100 a gateway, repeater or protocol converter?
faqs.a: No. It does not collect measurements, amplify a radio link, provide LTE connectivity or send MQTT records. These are functions of separately specified connected equipment.

faqs.q: Does it support every frequency between 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz?
faqs.a: That is not established by the published band references. Obtain the usable passband and RF performance record for the required version and operating frequencies.

faqs.q: Is it a galvanic isolator, directional coupler or flameproof connector transit?
faqs.a: The public H100 reference does not establish its internal topology or any of those specific protection functions. Request the product technical documentation; these component types and their approval conditions must not be treated as interchangeable.

faqs.q: Does fitting the H100 make a radio system intrinsically safe?
faqs.a: No such blanket claim is made. Any protection function requires the applicable certificate, marking and installation instructions for the exact configuration, together with an assessment of the complete equipment assembly.

faqs.q: Which certification should be requested for a classified area?
faqs.a: Specify the target jurisdiction, gas or dust group, area classification, temperature requirements and equipment arrangement. Obtain the corresponding certificate and installation conditions for the exact supplied configuration before selection; certification availability must be established for the proposed equipment duty.

faqs.q: How should insertion loss and port matching be specified?
faqs.a: State the operating band, reference impedance, cable and connector arrangement, permitted input power and test method. Agree acceptance values and compare measurements with the technical record for the supplied version.

faqs.q: Will it extend wireless range or improve coverage?
faqs.a: Range is a system result involving the radio, antenna, installation and environment. The coupling component must fit the RF budget; it is not specified as a booster or a guaranteed coverage improvement.

faqs.q: Does the IP68 reference apply to connected cables and antennas?
faqs.a: The published reference concerns the housing. Confirm immersion depth and duration, sealing and ratings for the supplied connector and cable assembly, with the connected equipment assessed separately.

faqs.q: Which temperature rating applies to the installed equipment?
faqs.a: The published H100 operating and storage reference is -40°C to +125°C. Confirm the supplied component limits and connected cable, antenna and equipment limits before using this reference in the assembly design.

faqs.q: Can components be connected or exchanged while powered?
faqs.a: Do not assume live connection, disconnection or hot swapping is permitted. Follow the exact equipment documentation and applicable site procedure for the supplied installation.

faqs.q: What is needed to assess an H100 configuration?
faqs.a: Provide radio and antenna references, operating band, RF budget, ports, cable lengths, mechanical layout, exposure, required approvals and quantity. Include an existing acceptance baseline for retrofit or replacement work.
